evidence: A fixed-completion funding requirement, conditional on reference mining and existing customer-budget scenarios. External equity top-ups are identified requirements, not committed funds. Financial ratios and welfare proxies are not market forecasts.
rules: Complete the prescribed physical path with dated external equity top-ups whenever retained cash and admissible capital credit are insufficient. Loan proceeds cannot fund operating deficits. Report first support year and cumulative new support.

Retain the established seed, five-year initial working buffer, capital accounting and finite worldwide service budgets. Extra machinery, continuing renewal and additional technical staffing are charged separately.

Compare identical productive paths. Credit substitutes financing; it does not create extra products, customer demand or a welfare benefit. Outside suppliers hold matched U term claims. Local U loan portions bear 2.5 percent real, other claims 3 percent.

Keep the existing 1.5 coverage, 70 percent pledgeable cash, 75 percent package lending, 25 percent of seed debt ceiling, two-year grace and 20-year amortization. New loans require positive 40-year incremental operating-value appraisal. Equity top-ups do not increase the fixed debt ceiling.

Initial monetary reserves cost 5 percent of the seed. Earned contributions are 20 percent of positive cash after debt service, toward one year of core imports plus 40 percent of U debt. No newly created U supplies foreign reserve assets.

All-equity completion is the monetary comparison. Additional U circulating balances must satisfy the inherited 0.5 percent annual positive-premium and 5 percent cumulative limits; replace rejected credit with explicit external equity. This is not a forecast of absolute inflation.

After funding current capital and operating buffers, cash is retained for the next year's known net requirement before distributing the surplus. This avoids paying dividends immediately before a predictable top-up. Longer optimization is not assumed.

Financial NPV includes all sponsor contributions and realized payouts. Liquid balances and reserves less remaining debt are shown separately as terminal book claims; no factory resale or perpetuity is credited.

Socioeconomic scenarios value final exports and resident services independently at half and full inherited prices, remove identified reserve transfers and resident payroll, and add resident opportunity costs. Research spillovers and strategic benefits enter only as required additional-net-benefit thresholds.
